zephyr-client-fixed.built_as: the fixed-memory client of overlays/t2g_client_fixed.conf with the idle wait and batching off (main stack 4480 bytes), its node wz_session_mcu::slot_node
zephyr-client-fixed.chain_misses: calls through a register (7 on the path of the chain), which the stack gate's reader does not follow; the firmware's own reading is 80 bytes over the chain (it was 76 before the node's set-up and its loop were two functions, and 24 before the connect manager's actions and a new row were built in the places they are kept, which took the dial off the longest chain and left the key matching under a query's answer, and 104 before the received handshake chain kept only the entries the build reads, which moved the path that sets the reading back to the dial, and 76 before the session's bundle was written in its slot field by field, which moved the path that sets the reading from the dial to the handshake's parse, and 108 before the receive decoded into a slot it was lent, 268 before the connect manager's actions were one buffer, and 424 before the dial handed the slot the function that makes the session's parameters, which took 500 from the chain and none from the reading, because the reading was on the planner's path; see the measured note), since the initial sequence number stopped taking the permutation's frame (CONFIG_WZ_INITIAL_SN_COMPACT) and the connect manager's planner call became a trait object, and the path that sets the reading was not identified
zephyr-client-fixed.measured: 2026-10-23, the T2G kit (CYT4BF M7) on its own Ethernet to a zenohd on the bench host; the stack line is the same in 7 of 7 runs, the GET figure is the median of 14 medians (0.320 to 0.471 ms) of 2000 queries for each of the node's two documents. The stack figures were re-read on 2026-10-27 after the not-a-Frame dispatch was split into decode, judge and engine steps (static chain 6,940, peak 6,060 in 2 of 2 runs, GETs inside their row; the tree before the split read 7,152 and 6,336, and the one before log_args 7,296 and 6,480): the decoded handshake message no longer sits in a frame under the engine's answer, and the worst chain is now the connect manager's dial path. After the SCE pin moved to 6dbfa6a521 the same build read static chain 6,372 and peak 5,880 in 2 of 2 runs (the engine's microstep buffers are sized to each document's state tree). On 2026-10-28 the five declarations a session with no allocator sends went through one dispatch, taking the arguments of their writer in place of a closure each (text 176,352 to 174,100 bytes): the worst chain reads 6,396 and the peak 5,904 in 1 of 1 run, 24 bytes over the row, 16 of them the enum the main frame now holds. On 2026-10-28 the initial sequence number became a compact function of the two zids (`CONFIG_WZ_INITIAL_SN_COMPACT`, which this image's overlay turns on): the Keccak permutation was the deepest frame of the chain, which fell 500 bytes to 5,896 (17 frames, 12 calls through a register not followed), and the kit's reading did not move, 5,904 in 1 of 1 run, GETs answered by a zenohd with the new origin. On 2026-10-28 the connect manager's `drive` and `ask` took the planner's call as a trait object (one copy each and not one per closure): the chain fell to 5,512 (the main frame 1,792 to 1,256) and the peak read 5,904 as before, in 1 of 1 run. On 2026-10-28 the dial handed the slot the function that makes the session's parameters (328 bytes, which each call between the dial and the slot had copied into its frame): the chain fell to 4,980 (`dial_expecting` 1,224 to 688), the bound to 6,084 (the worst path is now the planner's `open` and the peer entry, 1,000 and 1,080 bytes), and the peak read 5,904 as before, in 1 of 1 run; the main stack follows the bound, 8,320 to 8,128. On 2026-10-28 the connect manager's peer entry was built as the call's own result and started after it was in the table (`PeerEntry::new` no longer starts a local machine and moves it): the reading, which sat on the planner's path and not on the dial's, fell 656 bytes to 5,248 in 1 of 1 run, and the bound to 5,972 (the worst path is now the receive's lend of a declaration, 2,064 bytes, under a query's answer); the main stack follows, 8,128 to 8,000. On 2026-10-29 the connect manager's actions became one buffer that `drive` fills through `ask` and `take` reads in place (the six of them, about 300 bytes, had been a copy in `ask`, one in `drive` and one more for `take`), and `reconcile` put the rows in the list's order in place (it had held two copies of the table): the chain fell to 4,172 (the receive's, now) and the reading 1,000 bytes to 4,280 in 1 of 1 run; the bound stays 5,972, set by the receive's lend of a declaration. On 2026-10-29 the loop's node (448 bytes), factory (68) and host (36) were built in the storage's arena (`NodeStorage::run`, 576 bytes of `.bss`) and not held as locals of the main function (704 bytes of frame, from 1,256): the chain fell to 3,620, the reading 552 bytes to 3,728 in 1 of 1 run, the bound to 5,420; the main stack follows, 8,000 to 7,232. On 2026-10-29 the receive decoded a transport message into a slot its caller lends (`parse_unit_into`, `decode_unit_in` and `decide_unit_in` take the slot; they had passed the 720-byte message by value, and `parse_init` built it in a local of its own beside the caller's): the handshake's parse, 1,008 bytes of frame, is no longer the worst chain; the dial is (`reconcile`, `drive`, `dial_peer`, `dial_expecting` and the slot's `open`, 3,564 bytes over 7 frames), and the reading fell 88 bytes to 3,640 in 1 of 1 run. On 2026-10-29 four more changes of the same kind: the dial's link made in the slot's claim (`claim_with`; the 176-byte driver was held in several copies in `dial_expecting`, 688 bytes of frame, now 256), the receive's records decoded in the binding that lends them (`lend_declare` 2,064 bytes and `lend_push` 1,776 were three copies of the largest message a record can be; the generated `decode_into` writes it once), the key matcher's view of a key one array on this profile (256 bytes, where it was over 400) and the peer table's entry built in its row (`PeerEntry::init_in`, over the machine's `new_in_place`: the planner's `open` held the machine's kilobyte as a temporary, 1,008 bytes of frame, now 200): the chain 3,132, the bound 4,240 and the reading 3,208 in 1 of 1 run (it was 3,584 until the planner's, which the first dial runs through). On 2026-10-29 the session's bundle was written in the slot field by field (`SessionLinkActions::build_in`; the four handshake ext chains, 200 bytes each, were four slots of the frame of the function that built it, and the bundle had been a value of that function): the slot's `open` and what it calls fell from 1,068 bytes to about 570, the first tick's reading to 3,048, and the worst chain of direct calls is now the handshake's parse (the receive of an Init, 3,088 bytes), which sets the reading at 3,192 in 1 of 1 run. On 2026-10-29 a received handshake message kept the entries of the extensions the build reads and the header byte of every entry, where it had kept up to eight entries of 65 bytes (`ReceivedExtChain`: the inbound frame the decoder is lent fell by some 330 bytes, and `dispatch_unit_borrowed`, `parse_init` and the chain reader with it): the chain 3,024, the dial's path (the session pump's `build_in`, the engine's microsteps and `send_open_syn`) is the longest again, and the reading is 3,048 in 1 of 1 run, the first tick's. On 2026-10-29 the connect manager's actions (248 bytes, a local of `drive`) became a field of the manager, which lives in the node's storage (`RUN` 576 to 832 bytes, `.bss` 256 bytes more), and a new row was built in the table's row (`BoundedVec::push_with`, over a 152-byte value held twice in `reconcile`): the dial is off the longest chain, which is the key matching under a query's answer now (`dispatch_event_among`, `keyexpr_intersects_text`, `keyexpr_intersects_target`), 2,812 bytes, and the reading is 2,888 in 1 of 1 run, as many bytes as the single-thread zenoh-pico image's main thread. On 2026-10-29 the key matcher's view of a key was no longer built before it is used (`KeyChunks` keeps its 32 slots uninitialised and writes them as the chunks are found; the array was a second copy of the view, 256 bytes, in the frame of `keyexpr_intersects_target`): the chain is 2,784, the bound fell from 4,240 to 3,816 (the longest path under the observer is a query's reply through the network stack's send now) and the main stack from 5,696 to 5,120 bytes; the reading stayed inside its row, 2,888 within 16. On 2026-10-29 the node's set-up and its loop became two functions (`ClientNode::start`, inlined into the image's own `start`, whose frame is gone before the first round, and `RunningNode::drive`, the loop): the main function, which held the set-up's values under every call the loop makes, is 176 bytes of frame where it was 704, the loop is 400, the chain is 2,616, the bound fell from 3,816 to 3,352 (the dial is the longest path again) and the main stack from 5,120 to 4,480 bytes; the reading fell from 2,888 to 2,696 in 1 of 1 run, the first tick's and the receive's both under the single-thread zenoh-pico image's main thread. On 2026-10-30 the runtime took no interrupt lock (`CONFIG_WZ_SINGLE_CONTEXT`, which this image's overlay turns on): the chain fell from 2,616 to 2,560, the bound from 3,352 to 3,296 and the reading from 2,696 to 2,672 in 1 of 1 run. On 2026-10-30 the SCE pin moved to b1ede72108, which links the engine's Appendix D once for the program (the machine behind a reference to the engine's `MainLoop` and `Behaviour`, so two more rules of the contract and a shared copy whose procedures are frames of their own): the chain rose from 2,560 to 2,740 (14 frames), the bound from 3,296 to 3,764 and the reading from 2,672 to 3,000 in 1 of 1 run, and the main stack from 4,480 to 5,056 bytes, a quarter free over the bound. The SCE side works on those frames. On 2026-10-30 the SCE pin moved to f167223931 (packed rows, the engine taking events as numbers, its constructor and exit walk out of line): the chain fell from 2,740 to 2,536 (13 frames; the dial's `build_in` 600 to 80, `take_microstep` 232 to 120), the bound from 3,764 to 3,604 and the reading from 3,000 to 2,912 in 1 of 1 run (the same in the rebased tree), and the main stack from 5,056 to 4,864 bytes, a quarter free over the bound. On 2026-10-30 the SCE pin moved to 6ba84c3f37 (the entry walk bounded by two steps a level for a document with no parallel region): `run_turn` fell from 164 to 148 bytes, the bound from 3,604 to 3,588 and the main stack from 4,864 to 4,800 bytes; the chain and the reading did not move (2,536; 2,912). Later the same day the contract stopped counting an edge the code cannot take: `walk_entry`, `effective_target_states_on` and `is_in_final_state` take no Behaviour, and their calls through a register are the history and parallel procedures read from the document's tables, which a document without either does not carry (rule `walk-entry-tables`, with the premise that no function of the image is named for either); the hooks are called from `enter_states`, beside them. The bound fell from 3,588 to 3,476 and the main stack from 4,800 to 4,672 bytes; the chain and the reading, which are what ran, did not move. The same day three frames came down. The connect manager's `reconcile` put the rows in the list's order by `rotate_right(1)`, whose inlined library code held a row (152 bytes) and a buffer of its own: it moves a row by swaps of neighbours now, 448 bytes of frame to 328, the chain 2,536 to 2,416, the bound 3,476 to 3,356 and the main stack 4,672 to 4,480 bytes, and the reading at the end of the dial 2,608 to 2,488. The console's log functions rendered a line into a buffer returned by value (392 bytes in the callee and another in the caller: 832 bytes of frame, the largest of the image, under every log line): one buffer now. And the receive's reading of a handshake message was in the frame that also gave the engine the event of the admitted message (`dispatch_unit_in` kept the 400-byte decoded-message slot under the engine's answer, which wrote and sent the next message): the reading is its own function (`read_unit_in`) and the engine is given the event once it is gone. The kit's reading, which the console prints when it rises, fell from 2,896 (and 2,928 in a run) to 2,720 in 1 of 1 run: the deepest path the run reaches is the handshake's parse now (the receive of an Init: 2,672 bytes of frames in the call graph, the reading 48 over). On 2026-10-31 the SCE pin moved to b2ff4da1cb (the session id proven when it is compiled, and the engine's per-turn state kept in its shared core): the bound fell from 3,356 to 3,348 (8 bytes of frames on the longest path; which frame moved was not attributed), the main stack stays 4,480 bytes, and the chain and the reading did not move (2,416; 2,720 in 1 of 1 run). The text of this image fell 572 bytes, 143,356 to 142,784. On 2026-10-31 the SCE pin moved to 98803c0bc8 (ADR 0075: a machine keeps a delayed-send queue and a donedata slot only when its document fills them): the bound rose 8 bytes, 3,348 to 3,356 and the chain 8 bytes, 2,416 to 2,424 (which frame was not attributed; the stack gate held the 2,416 inside its tolerance of 128 until this row followed), the main stack stays 4,480 bytes, the reading did not move (2,720), and the text fell 96 bytes, 142,768 to 142,672.
